title: Nechemyah bar Baruch
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Moed Katan 16a has Ada Mari reporting Nechemyah bar Baruch, who reports R’ Chiyya bar Avin in R’ Yehudah’s name.
Shabbat 66b has Ada Mari reporting R’ Nachman bar Baruch in R’ Ashi bar Avin’s name. Dikdukei Soferim cites a manuscript reading according to which, Hyman says, it SHOULD READ as in Moed Katan 16a.

In Yevamot 102a, R’ Nechemyah [bar Baruch, according to the reading cited by Hyman from Tosafot Chad MiKamai] asks Rabbah a question. The continuation relates that the sages saw Rav Yehudah go out to the market wearing felt overshoes, with the number five attached [the supplied and printed qualifier זונות differs from the Bavli’s זוזי].

notes.text: The supplied זונות literally means harlots and does not fit the shoes. Earlier OCR suggested זוגות, pairs, but the checked continuation on 102b reads זוזי. The qualifier remains unresolved; the older “five pairs” is not treated as proven. Hyman’s two transmission chains are retained as variants.

No new primary scalar was returned. מרבה is of Rabbah, not Ravina. Supplied זונות literally harlots remains beside older machine זוגות, pairs, and the earlier recorded102b continuation זוזי; five pairs is not proven. דחויה is contextually read as saw, without a Hebrew repair. The number five, felt-overshoe context, two distinct transmission chains and bracketed Tosafot Chad MiKamai patronymic remain. Hyman says the manuscript reading SHOULD READ as in Moed Katan; this is stronger than merely agreeing. Uninspected abbreviated personal titles remain R-prime, while source full Rav Yehudah stays full.

Hyman’s print (vol. III, p. 927), like the supplied Hebrew, reads זונות in the shoe passage. The corresponding Yevamot 102b continuation has זוזי. Its context is one shoe worn over another, and the consulted English understands it as five pairs. The consulted Tosafot Chad MiKamai on 102a gives Nechemyah ben Baruch and reads Ameimar in the shoe example, where the consulted Bavli has Rav Yehudah. Dikdukei Soferim on Shabbat 66b, p. 141, note צ, explicitly reports Nechemyah and Chiyya for the Munich manuscript, beside a different transmission in its facing manuscript column. These are distinct readings of the transmission.
